name: Joseon buncheong
summary: Korean grey stoneware covered with white slip and a thin clear glaze. Potters stamp, carve, brush and paint the slip with bold and free patterns. The result is rustic, direct and lively.

philosophy.core_thesis: A plain grey stoneware gains life when a white slip is brushed, stamped or carved on it by a free hand with no fear of the rough.
design_principles: Cover the grey body with a thick white slip, by dipping or by brush, before the glaze.
Stamp small repeated flower or circle marks into the leather-hard clay and fill them with white slip.
Scratch a design through the white slip to the dark body (sgraffito) for a bold line.
Brush the slip fast with a straw brush to leave rhythmic marks on the surface.
Paint iron-brown lines on the slip, for fish, flowers and leaves, in a loose manner.
Cover the piece with a thin clear or grey-green glaze and fire at 1180 to 1250 °C.
Keep the form heavy and strong: a flat bottle, a round jar or a wide bowl.
anti_patterns: Delicate fine painting with a hard border
A thin refined body that shows translucency
A bright glossy glaze with coloured enamel

form.shape: Flat and round bottles, wide jars, bowls, dishes, and large storage jars with heavy shoulders.
form.profile: A firm, full belly with a short neck; the shape is round and slightly uneven.
form.foot_and_rim: A low, thick foot ring and a plain rim; the foot is often bare, with sand grains stuck to it.
form.proportion: Height 20 to 40 cm, a wall 6 to 12 mm thick, and the belly wider than the base by one half.
rules: Keep the wall thick and the form strong, not light.
Cover only part of the surface with slip, so the dark body stays as a contrast.
Let the brush marks and stamps vary along the piece.
Leave the foot unglazed and sandy.

bodies.rule: Use a grey, iron-rich stoneware that stays coarse and dark. The white slip, not the body, makes the pale colour.

forming.joins: A large jar is thrown in two parts and joined at the shoulder; handles and lugs are rare, and luted with slip when used.
forming.details: Fast brush strokes in white slip, small round stamp marks, and sand or spur marks on the base.

glaze.pattern: Large peonies cut through the slip, fish and lotus in iron brown, rings of stamped flowers, and free brush swirls.
glaze.gloss: Satin to glossy, about 40 to 70 GU, with a thin grey-green or clear glaze.
glaze.wear: The slip may crack and show the dark body; the glaze may pool in the cut lines and bring out the pattern.

palette.strategy: White slip on a grey body, with iron brown and a thin clear glaze; no bright colour at all.

firing.kiln: A wood-fired climbing kiln or a single-chamber kiln, with a loose reduction atmosphere.
firing.scale: Regional kilns in Gyeryongsan, Gwangju and Jeolla made ware for the court and for local government offices.
firing.signs: Sand or spur marks on the base, brush marks in the slip, and a thin glaze that thins on the high parts.

pieces.form: Flat bottle with a peony cut through white slip and a round neck
Jar with rings of stamped flowers filled with white slip
Bottle with a free iron-brown fish and lotus on a white ground
Wide bowl with a fast brush swirl of white slip inside

positive: heavy round jar, sand on the foot

canonical_works.work: Bottle with stamped and inlaid design

evidence.title: Buncheong bowl with a stamped bead design
Buncheong ritual vessel with brushed white slip

emotion.target_response: A warm, free ease: the viewer sees a brush and a hand with no fear and feels honest, lively craft.

use_cases: a rustic jar or bottle with a slip pattern
a museum label on early Joseon ceramics
a prompt for a free brush pattern on grey clay
avoid_when: the brief needs a thin, translucent or very white body
the brief needs fine, exact painting

modifiers.how: Use a finer stoneware, thin the glaze to clear green and inlay fine white and black lines.
Change to white porcelain with a clear glaze, remove all pattern and keep a plain round form.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Korean ceramics
